newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end down, feeders higher.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end down, feeders higher.

text.p: CME live cattle closed lower, pressured by sagging cash beef prices and active transferring of long February positions to April and June, traders said.
Feeder cattle futures closed with modest gains, but down from the contract highs set early in the session.

In live cattle, traders said packers have been reluctant to raise bids for feedlot cattle, which weighed on futures. Bids were steady at $65.00 per cwt Tuesday at High Plains feedlot, but cattle feeders passed them and priced cattle at $67.00 to $68.00.
Also, commercial firms were featured selling the February against speculative buying.

Traders said in the longer term, April may increase its premium over February because feedlots have marketed cattle ahead of schedule and eventually the supply of market-ready cattle will shrink. April closed at 66.825 cents per lb versus February's close of 65.850 cents.
Feeder cattle drew support from recent gains in cash prices, reflected by the sharp jump in the CME feeder cattle cash index. The latest index was up 0.65 cent at 69.20 cents per lb.

Live cattle closed down 0.300 to 0.075 cent per lb with February off the most at 65.850 cents. Feeder cattle were up 0.250 to 0.050 cent with January up 0.250 at 70.175 and March up 0.175 at 69.525. January set a contract high of 70.400 cents and March, a contract high of 70.000 during the session.
